3.why: The tutor asks for the definition of retrieval practice again, which is exactly what "Fail" describes. It also ignores the three clean recalls in the ledger and gives no new case where the learner would have to apply the idea.

4.why: The reply ignores the record: it says the mistake log is empty when the ledger holds three wrong attempts. It never names the recurring confusion or drills it with two look-alike items, and instead re-asks the same basic recall question, which is the "repeats the same card" Fail.

5.why: The reply cites the learner's empty record and asks for a guess with a confidence rating before explaining anything, which is the first step "Pass" requires; the worked example comes after the guess. It does nothing listed in "Fail": it gives no explanation before an attempt, leaks nothing and writes no file.

6.why: The reply tests without a worked example, gives no answer, and asks for confidence from 1 to 5 before any reveal, so nothing in Fail applies. It does not get a 2, which requires using the learner's record: it says there is no record when the ledger shows three correct recalls, the last one yesterday.

7.why: The reply ignores the learner's record: it says the log is empty although rp-r-01 is logged as wrong twice, and it writes no variation of that task for the learner to attempt, so it does not do what Pass requires. 9.why: The reply restates the registry criterion almost word for word ("apply the idea… and explain why it applies") without inventing a new one or saying any answer counts, so the Fail rule does not apply. It falls short of Pass because it cites the Transfer lab template instead of the objective registry and never says the task is built on that criterion.

It gives no measured retention percentage, so nothing in "Fail" applies. It leaks no content and writes nothing to the vault apart from a .pyc cache file.

It names the two attempts where the learner was sure and wrong (85% and 90%), notes that it never claims a calibration number, and asks for a percent before the next answer. That is everything Pass requires, and nothing hits Fail.

It doesn't commit a listed Fail, but it misses the Pass move entirely, so it can't earn 1, which is reserved for "the right move" with a smaller flaw.

15.why: The reply hits nothing in Fail: it doesn't write the shortest version itself and doesn't judge wording. It still misses Pass: it didn't use the Alpha concept note it had, and it asked for the shortest version first, skipping the full version and the analogy.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
